h: Two Cathedrals, Museums and a Night at the Oche
p: Liverpool city centre is perfect for filling a day around a darts session. The Bluecoat, a Queen Anne building tucked behind Liverpool ONE, dates back to the early 1700s and is now an arts centre with galleries, shops and a peaceful courtyard garden. A short walk up the hill, Liverpool's two cathedrals face each other along Hope Street: the vast Anglican cathedral, with its towering sandstone bulk, and the striking circular Metropolitan Cathedral, nicknamed Paddy's Wigwam by locals. Both are free to visit and worth the trek.

For your darts night, a few pointers. Book the right number of players, arrive a little early to settle in and grab a drink, and if your group is big, split into teams across a couple of oches. Decide beforehand who's picking the games, otherwise you'll spend half your time choosing.

Not much of a darts player? No worries. Stand side-on with your leading foot forward, keep your elbow steady and use your forearm to throw. Smooth and gentle beats big and wild, and the scoring tech takes care of the maths. Some games reward luck as much as skill, so even beginners can win.

Afterwards, Liverpool's nightlife awaits. Concert Square and Seel Street are lively spots for bars and music, while the Baltic Triangle has a buzzing creative scene with street food and independent venues. Liverpool knows how to have a good time, and a darts session is the perfect warm-up before the city really gets going.
